title: Finite-type capture on a compact open inside an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $V$ an affine open, and $K\subseteq V$ a quasi-compact open [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $H$ be a quasi-coherent module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent] whose restriction to $K$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. There exists a quasi-coherent finite-type module $Q$ on $V$ and a monomorphism $\iota:Q\to H|_V$ such that $\iota|_K$ is an isomorphism. No module on a larger union is asserted.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PF (label lemma-extend), proof: affine finite-numerator argument using Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PF

proof.text: Choose n and a map from the finite free sheaf on V to H restricted to V which is epimorphic after restriction to K. This is exactly the finite-numerator selection step; it asserts no submodule and no monomorphism.

Construct Q as the abelian image of this finite free map, namely the kernel of its cokernel map. The slice/open-subscheme equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels. Apply Mathlib's existing isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isLeftAdjoint theorem directly to transport the source and target to the open subscheme, and to transport the resulting image back; the unit isomorphism identifies that inverse transport with Q. No duplicate slice/open equivalence theorem is declared. The proved source-library quasi-coherent kernel and cokernel closure theorems therefore give quasi-coherence of Q. The finite standard basis of the free sheaf maps through the epimorphic image factorization to global generators of Q. Its local-generators data proves finite type, without using the general finite-type epimorphic-image theorem. The image inclusion is monic by the kernel construction.

Restrict the image inclusion to K. The shared moduleOverMap finite-limit-preservation instance preserves its monomorphism. The restricted finite free map factors through it and is epi, so epi_of_epi_fac makes the restricted inclusion epi too. In the abelian category of module sheaves a morphism both mono and epi is an isomorphism. This proves the required witness with no localization-injectivity or inverse-gluing lemma. Empty K and n = 0 are covered by the same categorical argument.

proof_origin.place: Properties, Lemma 01PF, final paragraph; Lean recombination via the abelian image of a finite free numerator map, with source-library kernel/cokernel closure and shared exact open restriction. Repair: removed the duplicate private slice/open equivalence theorem and directly applied Mathlib quasi-coherent pushforward transport in the image proof.

mathlib_searches.results: LocalGeneratorsData, GeneratingSections and IsFiniteType results; no finite-type affine capture or union theorem.
Mathlib has no finite-type affine submodule capture; source FiniteTypeExtension is for ideal sheaves, not arbitrary modules.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_affine_capture
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V : X.affineOpens) (K : X.Opens)
    (hK : IsCompact (K : Set X)) (hKV : K ≤ V.1)
    (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) [H.IsQuasicoherent]
    [(H.over K).IsFiniteType] :
    ∃ Q : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V.1),
      Q.IsQuasicoherent ∧ Q.IsFiniteType ∧ ∃ (ι : Q ⟶ H.over V.1),
        Mono ι ∧ IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overMap (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
          (homOfLE hKV)).map ι)
